blockingFindings: Sprint-level dependency granularity contradicts the stage-level admission order and would over-serialize early backend/integration work. openspec/sprints/sprints.json encodes only whole-sprint `requires` (SP04, SP05 require SP01; SP06 requires SP01+SP04; SP09 requires SP03, SP05, SP06, SP07, SP08), and openspec/sprints/verify.py validates only that graph. But SP01 bundles atomic-prepare/atomic-accept, rp01-mc02, rp01-mc03, rp01-full and f0 into one sprint, so under the machine register SP04 (f0a/f1), SP05 (i2) and SP06 (f2) cannot start until rp01-full (the complete challenge/operator/theorem/signing map over 277+72+8+8+3+5 rows) closes. This contradicts ROADMAP.md ('Language and native feasibility work can progress independently'), REPORT-RECONCILIATION-2026-09-07.md ('full RP01 ... is not a prerequisite for the unchanged fixed-instance F2'; topological order puts F0a/F1/F2/F3 before general extensions), the register's stage `requires` (f0/f0a/f1/f2/i2 do not require rp01-full) and README.md's own prose ('SP01's atomic, subset, full design and F0 tasks can close independently'). Worse, SP09.1 'Close atomic F3 before extending it' sits in a sprint whose register prerequisites include SP07 (all 277 ACTUS fixtures in semantic form) and SP08 (all 72 DeFi rows + DA01-DA24 + intents), while README.md says 'SP09 may prepare and close atomic F3 after SP05/SP06 while extended language work continues' and the register's f3 stage requires only atomic-accept, i2, f2, f1. A dispatcher following the charter's 'first eligible task in dependency order' on sprints.json would delay the first non-mock Preview PCD acceptance (F3) behind the entire financial corpus, which is exactly the formalization-before-acceptance sequencing the program forbids. Required fix: either split SP01 (atomic+subsets+F0 vs rp01-full) and SP09 (atomic F3 vs mandatory extension) into separately registered sprints, or add task/stage-level `requires` to sprints.json that verify.py checks against reportReconciliation.stageAdmission.stages, and make README.md prose and the register agree.
nonblockingFindings: Coverage crosswalk is package-granular, not requirement-granular: every requirement in openspec/sprints/coverage.json lists the owning package's entire sprint set (e.g. MC04 'Durable one-time consumption' -> SP01, SP03, SP04, SP05, SP09, SP11 although only SP09 realistically owns it; MC08 'Scope and release claims' -> SP01, SP02, SP08, SP12). verify.py's ownership check therefore passes trivially and cannot detect a requirement that no sprint task actually addresses. Assign one primary closing sprint per requirement (and optional contributing sprints) so the crosswalk has diagnostic value.

Lean-versus-K formal contract not fully reconciled: proposal.md and README.md replace planned `lake` builds with `formal/k/run.py prove --claims`, and the register commands were updated, but openspec/changes/mc04-ledger-correspondence-and-consumption/tasks.md 3.2 still says 'Run Lean without sorry or undeclared axioms', MORIARTY-COMPLETION-PROGRAM.md still says 'Formal outputs use pinned Lean toolchains ... where the package specifies Lean', and the charter/register extensionOwnership paths still list formal/Correspondence.lean, ContractProperties.lean and IntentRefinement.lean while SP09's file map creates formal/correspondence.md and no .lean. Implementers cannot tell whether a Lean bridge is required, optional or retired; state it once in the charter and update MC04 3.2.

Native path naming diverges across artifacts: MC03 tasks.md and the register commands use experiments/moriarty-native-ivc-r3/revision-01/…, SP06 creates experiments/moriarty-native-ivc-r3/successor/…, and SP04 places P1/P2/P3 under experiments/moriarty-ledger-adapter/probes/ although the reconciliation assigns native export to MC03 and only the finalizer/verifier port to MC04. The register acknowledges MC03 commands are 'legacy proposed entrypoints', but SP01.5 only mentions reconciling lake commands. Add explicit reconciliation of revision-01 vs successor and probe ownership to SP01.5 to prevent duplicate directories and split ownership of the export shim.

Shared-path writer serialization does not cover new successor/K files: SP03, SP07 and SP08 all modify experiments/moriarty-language/formal/k/moriarty.k, and SP07/SP08 are independent siblings, yet the charter's cross-package ownership list and register extensionOwnership.paths contain only atomic-era paths (spec/grammar.ebnf, src/evaluate.ts, …). Extend the path list with spec/successor/*, src/successor/*, formal/k/* so the 'serialize writers of shared paths' rule applies.

SP12.1 omits developer-flow scenarios required by ROADMAP.md MC08 and REPORT-RECONCILIATION step 7: revoked-key/spec, activation-window and consumption-preserving migration demonstrations (SP12.1 lists only loan/swap, rejected intent, stale observation, unavailable witness, pending redemption, restart, conflict). SP09.3 tests these at the acceptance layer but the MC08 developer demonstration would be incomplete.

Granularity of SP07.3 ('Implement all 277 pinned fixtures … necessary versioned Core extensions') and SP08.2 (six economic families in one task) is not honest as written; README.md instructs splitting large families into independently reviewable packets, but the sprint contracts do not pre-partition by contract type/family or name the per-batch exit evidence. Pre-list the batches (e.g. per ACTUS executable type) so progress and resource charging are legible.

Resource statement drift: README.md 'Resource, review and stop rules' refers to 'the historical eight-hour envelope', while openspec/moriarty-completion-program.json amendments raise master minutes to 850 and MC01 reservation to 385 min/13 dispatches versus the charter table's 50/4. The plan should cite the live register figures or explicitly say the charter table is historical.

coverage.json sourceDigests pins openspec/REPORT-RECONCILIATION-2026-09-07.md and docs/research/2026-09-06-actus-defi-design-study.md as 'stale planning source' checks. Both are living planning documents; any future reconciliation edit will fail verify.py. Either scope the digest check to the immutable inventories (CSV files) or document that reconciliation edits require a coverage.json re-pin.

SP02 verification command `node experiments/moriarty-language/src/cli.ts check …` executes a TypeScript source with plain node; the packet's stack builds via npm run build. Point the entry point at the built artifact or a package.json script so the first executable packet does not inherit a non-runnable command.

SP03.3 'Discharge the selected mechanized claims' does not enumerate which of coverage.json formalAdditions (finite termination, type preservation, determinism, progress-or-rejection, elaboration/evaluator correspondence) are required for the SP03 exit gate versus deferred; type preservation and evaluator correspondence are not natural K reachability claims, so the packet must name the bridge or mark them open. Also consider whether the narrow partial-payment K slice (DEFI-LANGUAGE-DESIGN step 4) can start on the existing atomic Core rather than waiting for SP02's complete successor frontend behind rp01-full.

The first concrete step (SP01.1) is acceptable: it starts from existing build/test commands, inspects before prescribing the input-boundary fix, and produces openspec/sprints/execution/SP01.md. Note that the very first action is authoring that packet; no runnable correction exists in this candidate, which is consistent with the stated planning-only scope.
